items.text: The riff that opens 'Ye Entrancemperium' was lifted from an unfinished Mayhem track that sits on a bootleg.
items.why: "The opening guitar riff to 'Ye Entrancemperium' is taken from an unnamed Mayhem song ... A recording of this unfinished track can be found on the Mayhem bootleg Ha Elm Zalag."
Infobox and Lead "May 19, 1997". Note the pack disagrees with itself: Release says "released on 8 July 1997 through Candlelight Records".

items.text: October to December 1996, Grieg Hall, Bergen, Norway

items.why: Infobox "Producer: Eirik Hundvin, Ihsahn and Samoth".

items.text: Ihsahn (vocals, guitar, synthesizer), Samoth (guitar), Alver (bass), Trym (drums and percussion)
items.why: Emperor: Ihsahn "vocals, guitar; synthesizer"; Samoth "guitar"; Alver "bass"; Trym "drums and percussion".

items.text: The liner notes credit Mayhem guitarist Euronymous all the same, though he had died three years earlier, before the album was made.
items.why: "Euronymous is credited in the album liner notes, even though he was murdered three years before the album was written and recorded." "all the same" leans on the hook for context.

items.text: A 1996 EP called Reverence came out ahead of the album as its teaser, and it included 'The Loss and Curse of Reverence'.
items.why: "In 1996, the EP Reverence, which included the track 'The Loss and Curse of Reverence', was released as a teaser for the album."

items.text: Pytten handled the engineering and production.
Yens and David Palser did the sleeve photography, Stephen O'Malley did the sleeve design, and Christophe Szpajdel made the illustrations and logo.
items.why: Photography, illustration and logo credits match, but the pack credits sleeve design to both "Stephen O'Malley" and "N. A. P."; the sentence gives it to O'Malley alone.

items.text: Set against In the Nightside Eclipse, the band's previous album, this one plays faster and leans harder on guitar.
items.why: "In contrast to the band's previous album, In the Nightside Eclipse, Anthems showcases a faster, more guitar-driven performance".

items.text: There are fewer keyboards, more clean singing and blast beats in the drums.
items.why: "less usage of keyboards and more clean singing and blast-beat style drumwork".

items.text: In 1998 a remastered version came out with the three Reverence tracks that had not made the album.
items.why: "In 1998, the album was remastered and re-released with the three non-album tracks from Reverence."

items.text: The band also made a promo video for 'The Loss and Curse of Reverence'.
items.why: "The band made a promotional video for 'The Loss and Curse of Reverence'." The pack gives no date for it.

items.text: It is an orchestral version of 'Inno a Satana', so what you hear is an orchestra.
items.why: Pack only says "orchestral version of 'Inno a Satana'". "so what you hear is an orchestra" is the writer's inference; the pack does not say a real orchestra plays.

missed: What the record sounds like beyond the comparison: crisper production, more variety in Ihsahn's vocals, guitar interplay between Ihsahn and Samoth, more complex melodic keyboards (AllMusic); lyrics moving from nature and Satanic themes towards mystical ones; the back cover line "Emperor performs Sophisticated Black Metal Art exclusively".
